Title: Developing scaling-up process to produce haloalkaliphilic bacteria inoculum for industry-deployment to treat alkaline wastes from refining alumina
Description: Australia's alumina sector is facing multi-billion dollars of liability to rehabilitate thousands of hectares of polluting bauxite residue (or red mud), which have already been accumulated in landscapes of Queensland, Northern Territory and Western Australia. This project aims to develop a process to effectively treat waste generated from refining alumina using haloalkaliphilic bacteria, which is a special type of bacteria. The production of aluminium produces a variety of bauxite waste products, some of which can be highly alkaline in nature. The ability to treat this waste would benefit resource companies by making alumina refinement more sustainable.

Title: Developing Spatial Adaptive Imaging for Clinics
Description: This project aims to generate a new technology called Australian Made Spatial Adaptive Imaging (SAI), capable of surpassing the current gold-standards for high resolution imaging, including single cell imaging and other high resolution microscopy techniques. By pushing the boundaries of imaging technology, this project has the potential to significantly improve clinical diagnostics and treatments, offering a new level of detail and understanding in medical imaging that could benefit patients in Australia and around the world.

Title: Development of a mini-gut reactor system for functional screening of gut microbiome modulators
Description: This project aims to develop a testing platform (mini-gut reactor) that can reduce the time taken to functionally test gut microbiome and help diagnosis and improve overall health. The gut microbiome refers to microorganisms living in the human digestive track which play a crucial role in human health. The ability to assess its function quickly and accurately is vital for advancing medical research and treatment. This project has the potential to transform the way gut health is managed and understood, with significant implications for healthcare in Australia and globally.

Title: Development of non-invasive imaging tools to idendify recombinant protein expression in plant based molecular farming
Description: Traditional meat production systems are unsustainable, using over 60 per cent of all the food we grow to feed the animals we eat. The future of meat is cultured but producers are struggling with high cost and low availability of the ingredients they need. Pharmaceutical, alternative food protein and nutraceutical sectors are investing in plant-based molecular farming (PBMF), where plants are used as protein factories. This project aims to develop a 3D scanner that can non-invasively detect and analyse the presence of food-grade recombinant proteins in plant leaves. This technology is crucial for the field of PBMF as it would allow for the optimisation and quantification of protein yield in leaves without damaging the plants. The project will utilise a unique 3D hyperspectral scanner at the Australian Plant Phenomics Facility. The scanner will identify the expression of these proteins, which are important for various applications, including pharmaceuticals and food products.

Title: Direct air capture of carbon dioxide and water to enable sustainable biomanufacturing
Description: The uncontrolled use of fossil fuels has resulted in a graduate increase in atmospheric CO2 concentration and anthropogenic global warming. To address this issue, ‘negative emission technologies’, particularly direct air capture (DAC) are coming into focus globally. This project aims to design and build solar-powered DAC units capable of capturing CO2 producing water, thereby aligning well with Australia’s climate commitments. DAC technology aims to extract CO2 and water directly from the atmosphere. This process is powered by solar energy, making it a renewable and sustainable method.

Title: Enabling the Lithium economy by creating vale-added product(s) for energy storage market
Description: Currently, Australia contributes to around half of the world’s lithium production for a global market of USD $3.83 billion. However, we most typically export lithium ores overseas for development into value-added products only to purchase the technology (e.g. batteries, supercaps) back at a higher price. This project aims to create next-generation, value-added products from lithium for the emerging energy storage market. The significance of this project lies in its potential to contribute to the lithium economy by creating high-value products such as lithium-ion capacitors (LICs), which offer a combination of battery-like energy density and supercapacitor-like power density. Battery technology is a vital part of the renewable energy mix and can be scaled from a personal household device up to grid-scale storage.

Title: Establishing Vision-BaDGE anti-VEGF DNA therapy for age-related macular degeneration
University: The University of New South Wales
Description: The project aims to develop a DNA-based therapy called ‘Bionic array Directed Gene Electrotransfer’ (BaDGE®) to treat wet age-related macular degeneration (wetAMD) and related vision disorders. Age-related macular degeneration is a leading cause of vision loss in the elderly, and the development of this therapy could provide a significant breakthrough in the treatment of these conditions. It holds promise not only for improving the quality of life for individuals affected by wetAMD in Australia but also has global implications for the treatment of vision disorders.

Title: Geothermal Cities: Transfomring Urban Energy Supply with Innovative and Cost- Effective Shallow Geothermal Systems
University: The University of New South Wales
Description: This project seeks to tackle the pressing challenge of energy affordability and the climate crisis in densely populated urban areas. It aims to harness the untapped potential of geothermal energy (heat derived from the earth’s interior) using ‘shallow geothermal systems’ which are both cost-effective and efficient. The successful implementation of shallow geothermal systems, which use stable temperatures near the earth’s surface to heat and cool buildings, could significantly impact energy sustainability in Australia, offering a reliable and affordable energy source while also contributing to global climate change mitigation efforts.

Title: High resolution cortical recording for the prediction and prevention of epileptic seizures
Description: Worldwide, more than 30 per cent of the people living with epilepsy are drug resistant. For many patients the anxiety associated with the unpredictability of seizures represents one of the primary burdens of the disease. This project is working to develop an implantable device that can monitor brain activity with high precision. Their aim is to predict and prevent epileptic seizures, which could also lead to a breakthrough in effectively treating depression and anxiety without the use of drugs. This technology has the potential to transform the lives of individuals suffering from epilepsy by providing a drug-free treatment option. It's a significant advancement not only for Australian healthcare but also for global medical practices.

Title: High-yield, low-cost manufacturing of quantum magnetic field sensors
University: The University of New South Wales
Description: This project aims to develop a low-cost manufacturing process for superconducting quantum magnetic sensors, capable of non-invasive geological mapping of resource deposits. The technology uses new methods in creating high-temperature superconductors with a helium ion beam to directly make the superconducting device. The sensors can detect magnetic fields in different ways, either as a vector magnetometer or as a magnetic gradiometer, which allows for mapping magnetic fields deep inside the earth. By identifying and mapping Australia’s primary resources, this project can practically enhance the work of mineral companies. A more efficient resources sector will be critical to building technology to drive down emissions.

Title: Improving diabetes treatment with a point-of-care device to objectively assess disease
Description: Over 1.2 million Australians have diabetes, costing $2.7 billion annually. Poor blood flow in the feet is a major complication and the leading global cause of chronic foot ulcers and foot amputations. However, clinicians lack good devices to help them assess blood flow. This project aims to develop a new medical device to accurately measure blood flow in patients. This innovation aims to enhance the treatment of diabetes by providing clinicians with objective data to inform their treatment decisions. This device has the potential to revolutionise treatment protocols, ensuring that diabetic patients receive the most appropriate and effective care.

Title: Improving flotation benefication of minerals
Description: Flotation is the most widely used process for extracting minerals from their ores and uses water to either repel or attract minerals. This project aims to improve on the current flotation metal recovery process, which is crucial to significantly reduce processing time and metal loss. Importantly, improving flotation methods is important for products like rare earth elements which can have very low mineral concentrations. The project is expected to yield increased flotation recovery and product grade, providing valuable knowledge for full-scale design and potentially boosting production and export income from license fees.

Title: Industrially viable manufacturing for next generation solar cells
Description: This project aims to continue to build on and improve Australia’s solar cell industry by creating a manufacturing process that is both sustainable and efficient. It seeks to tackle the challenges of solvent toxicity and the cost and availability of critical materials, which are significant hurdles in the production of next-generation solar cells. By addressing these issues, the project intends to produce solar cells that are not only more efficient and cost-effective but also environmentally friendly, aligning with the global shift towards renewable energy sources and reduced greenhouse gas emissions.

Title: Lithium-ion Battery Recycling and Reclamation
Description: This project is focused on advancing lithium-ion battery recycling and reclamation. Lithium-ion batteries are essential in everything from smartphones to electric vehicles, and as the world transitions to net zero their demand will only increase. Australia's development of on-shore capabilities to ensure the battery’s components can be reintegrated into the battery supply chain or repurposed across various industries, preventing harmful chemicals being released into the environment through landfill is crucial.

Title: Low-Emission Carbon Dioxide Recycling Technology for Concrete Masonry Production
University: The University of New South Wales
Description: This project is pioneering a new CO2 capture technology for use in new low-emission concrete masonry. This project aims to create a new market for captured CO2 from industry sectors with hard-to-abate emissions. The captured CO2 will be used to make a new low-emission concrete masonry. This project aims to support a more sustainable construction industry, reducing the carbon emissions that come from making one of the most common building materials.

Title: Manufacture and agronomic assessment for polymer-free lignite derived slow-release fertiliser (SRF)
Description: This project aims to design and manufacture slow-release fertilisers (SRFs) characterised with high efficiency and sustained slow-release of nutrients. The project's goal is to design and manufacture these SRFs without the use of polymers, which are traditionally used in such fertilisers to control nutrient release rates. There are environmental benefits in retaining more nitrogen in soil for a longer period as nitrogen losses and run off is a pressing issue in agriculture. Using lignite as ‘scaffolding’ may allow the plants to access more of the nitrogen in the SRF.

Title: Market-relevant Rechargeable Aluminium Battery Prototyping
Description: Battery storage is essential for Australia to shift to lower emissions electricity systems. Despite being well endowed with world-class battery minerals Australia’s battery industry is at the low end of the battery value chain. This project aims to bring a new type of rechargeable battery to the market. By leveraging a patented graphene processing technique developed at The University of Queensland, the project seeks to create aluminium batteries that are not only rechargeable but also more efficient and potentially cheaper than current options.

Title: Mining with muons: muon tomography methods for site exploration and safety management
Description: This project aims to conduct the first underground survey using muon tomographic at a mine site using Australian-developed technology. Muons are elementary particles generated through cosmic rays and used to peer inside dense or dangerous objects and environments. This groundbreaking survey method will significantly enhance site exploration and safety management by providing detailed 3D density maps of underground structures. The generation of 3D modelling at mine sites will allow industry to identify mineral deposits and oil reservoirs without the need to enter the spaces physically.

Title: NanoVibeH2: High Frequency Sound Wave Electrolytic Enahancement for Efficient Green Hydrogen Production
University: The Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology (RMIT)
Description: This project aims to develop a technology known as the NanoVibeH2, which uses high frequency sound waves to efficiently produce green hydrogen. Electrolysis involves electricity running through water with two electrodes to split water molecules into oxygen and hydrogen gases, which appear as bubbles. This technology offers a promising way to tap into a plentiful supply of cheap hydrogen fuel for transportation and other sectors, which could radically reduce carbon emissions and help fight climate change.

Title: Olives the Australia Way - A new style of table olive using a novel debittering process
Description: Olives are a healthy product due to the presence of anti-oxidants, vitamins and anti-cancer compounds. Current commercial methods to reduce the bitterness of olives use lye and/or fermentation whereolives are stored in an acidic brine solution. These industrial processes result in much wastewater, and produce olives high in salt that is devoid of natural flavours. This project is focused on developing a new style of olive using a patented and novel process. to remove bitterness from olives quickly and effectively whilst maintaining high quality. The goal is to provide consumers with a healthy table olive that contains less salt whilst preserving the natural fresh flavours and healthy compounds. The process also offers the possibility of using the olive brine extracts for a range of health-related products, such as nutraceuticals or new food ingredients.

Title: On-sun testing of thermo-photocatalytic water-splitting for hydrogen production
Description: This project aims to advance clean hydrogen production technology via photocatalysis, which is a method of harnessing sunlight to drive chemical reactions. Green hydrogen is a clean fuel, and its production through such innovative means is crucial for Australia's energy future and the global shift towards sustainable energy sources. The project is expected to fast-track the technology from lab-scale to a beta prototype-scale reactor tested in real sun conditions, moving it closer to meeting the demand for green hydrogen from industries that are hard to decarbonise.

Title: Ore-sand: a circular economy solution to reduce mineral wastes and produce alternative construction materials
Description: This project aims to tackle two major sustainability challenges in the mining industry: managing tailings waste in mining operations and reducing the need for natural sand extraction. The project’s innovative approach involves developing mineral processing techniques to create a new product called ore-sand, which can be used in construction and other industries. This project demonstrates a move towards a more sustainable, circular economy by repurposing by-products from mineral mining.

Title: Proof of concept cattle tick vaccine trial for commercial adoption
Description: Cattle ticks are members of the Rhipicephalus microplus species and are responsible for $US22-30 billion in losses to cattle industries world-wide. In Australia, beef producers are losing $128.2 million every year due to tick related losses. This project aims to validate the efficacy of novel tick vaccines. These vaccines are designed to significantly reduce the presence of ticks in economically important cattle breeds. The project is part of a broader effort to enhance agricultural productivity and animal health, with potential benefits including improved cattle welfare and reduced reliance on chemical tick treatments.

Title: Rapid development of new medical treatment compounds from radioactive mine waste
Description: This project aims to identify a new source of cancer therapy medicines, called ‘radiopharmaceuticals’, which can be extracted from existing uranium mining waste. The process involves sourcing samples from radioactive waste at legacy mine sites, determining optimal extraction protocols through tests on synthetic and simulated compounds and then verifying these protocols on actual radioactive waste samples. Australia has the world’s largest uranium reserves and is the world’s third largest producer of uranium. Finding uses for uranium ore tailing and waste rock will assist industry to operate in a more sustainable way.

Title: Revolutionising Agriculture: Innovative Encapsulation Technologies for a Sovereign Supply Chain
Description: The global demand for animal-sourced foods continues to increase, but the livestock industry faces the challenge of high feed costs, which account for approximately 70 per cent of the total production expenses. Enzymes have become critical feed additives in the livestock industry, playing an essential role in improving animal performance, reducing feed conversion rates, and reducing mortality. This project focuses on enhancing Australia’s livestock industry and establishing sovereign supply chain capability, by developing a process that can encapsulate and deliver enzymes to livestock sustainably. The encapsulation technology aims to improve the stability and bioavailability of bioactive ingredients, which are crucial for animal performance and health.

Title: Sensing the unseen: Advanced hydrogen gas sensor
Description: As the use of hydrogen gas as a clean and sustainable energy carrier continues to grow, hydrogen sensors will play a critical role in ensuring its safe and efficient use. Hydrogen is naturally colourless and odourless, making it difficult to detect leaks or other hazards. This project is focused on developing a novel sensor for hydrogen gas detection, which will be assisted by artificial intelligence. The new sensor aims to offer higher sensitivity, faster response times and cost-effectiveness compared to current sensors. This sensor could be crucial for monitoring hydrogen in facilities where it's produced, stored, transported or used, enhancing safety and efficiency.

Title: Single-shot anti-fertility vaccine for pigs
Description: Boar taint is an objectionable odour correlated with androsterone (a male hormone) and skatole (a by-product of intestinal bacteria in males and females) that is often perceived during the cooking of pork and can also affect the flavour of meat and is a major consumer complaint. For centuries, pigs have been castrated to prevent boar taint which limits productivity and increases animal welfare concerns of commercial pork production. This project aims to develop a safe and effective vaccine for long-term hormonal control in pigs. The vaccine is expected to be a single-shot solution that produces long-term antibodies, reducing sex hormone levels in pigs and allowing for more efficient metabolism of skatole. The benefits include humane and sustainable pork production, reduced feed requirements and less waste compared to traditional castration methods, as immunised pigs convert food into body weight more efficiently.

Title: Sustainable metal extraction and recovery from metal-containing waste for renewable energy transition and circular economy
Description: This project aims to commercialise a process that recovers valuable metals from e-waste and spent lithium-ion batteries sustainably. The project seeks to minimise environmental impact and align with Australia's commitment to a circular economy, which emphasises sustainable consumption, production and waste reduction. This project is expected to contribute to Australia's economic growth by creating high-demand products while reducing mineral waste and supporting the transition to renewable energy.

Title: Targeting the Kv1.3 potassium channel to treat chronic kidney disease
Description: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a major public health problem, with more than 2 million Australians living with the disease, which is associated with adverse outcomes of kidney failure, cardiovascular disease and premature death. The project is focused on developing a therapy that targets the Kv1.3 potassium channel, a specific type of potassium channel found in the membranes of cells, which plays a role in the function of various tissues, including the kidneys, with the aim of treating CKD. This approach represents a novel strategy in the fight against CKD, which currently has limited treatment options beyond kidney transplantation and dialysis.

Title: Toward a rapid antibody test (RAT) for phosphine resistant insect pests of stored grain
Description: Phosphine fumigation is the mainstay of insect pest control in stored grain, making it essential to international trade and global food biosecurity, a role threatened by phosphine resistant pests. This project aims to create a Rapid Antibody Test (RAT) that can quickly identify every resistance variant in every species of pest insect of stored grain resistant to phosphine. The presence of these resistant insects can lead to significant crop loses; therefore, timely action is crucial to manage them. The technology developed could reinforce Australia's position as a leader in postharvest grain handling and improve the country's competitive stance in international markets.

Title: Towards Non-invasive Pathology using Thermal Imaging Spectroscopy for Skin Cancer Diagnosis
Description: Skin cancer is a prevalent issue in Australia, with 2 out of 3 Australians being diagnosed with it in their lifetime, and one Australian dying every 5 hours. This project aims to develop a non-invasive method to detect skin cancer using a thermal imaging spectroscopy. This camera-based technology will allow for the early detection and categorisation of suspicious skin lesions, potentially improving the accuracy and speed of cancer diagnosis. This can save the time of dermatologists and can also be very useful as an opportunistic screening service in areas with limited access to specialised medical facilities like rural and remote locations.

Title: Transforming Australian regions for sustainable development: a novel approach to efficient recovery for cleaning contaminated sites
Description: This project aims to develop an environmentally friendly and cost-effective technology to recover valuable metals and eliminate harmful compounds from contaminated soils and sediments. The project is part of a larger effort to commercialise processes that recover valuable metals from various forms of waste, such as e-waste and spent lithium-ion batteries, in a sustainable manner. The ongoing rehabilitation of mine sites across Australia is an important issue for the social licence of the resources industry along with cultural impact for traditional landowners. Boosting the value of effective mine site closure will mitigate the costs and promote holistic life of site management.

Title: Utilising alternative cytokine receptor signalling for enhanced cell-based cancer immunotherapy
Description: This project is focused on developing new cell-based therapies by leveraging alternative cytokine receptor signalling pathways. Cytokine receptor signalling pathways refers to the complex communication process between cells that can be harnessed to trigger an immune response against cancer cells. The aim is to create more effective treatments for cancer, which remains one of the most challenging diseases to treat.

Title: Value Adding Natural Zeolite Resources: Enhanced Anaerobic Digestion for Biogas Production and Nutrient Management
Description: This project aims to improve biogas production using large-scale anaerobic digesters. These digesters break down organic matter like manure or food waste and the process is enhanced by the addition of natural zeolite. Zeolite can capture nutrients like ammonium, potassium, and phosphate, which are beneficial for wastewater treatment and reducing fertilizer consumption. A more efficient process for digestion means more nutrients can be effectively recovered and used again for other purposes like producing renewable energy.

Title: World's first chemical antibody-based intraoperative diagnostic platform for surgical pathology
Description: Cancer ranks as the second-leading cause of death worldwide. During cancer surgery, analysing tissue samples is crucial for detecting any remaining cancer cells and the spread of cancer to lymph nodes. This project aims to develop a tool that surgeons can use during surgery to quickly obtain precise information about internal organs while the patient is still in the operating room. This platform will revolutionise cancer surgical pathology by enabling real-time treatment decisions that are accurate and precise.

Title: MiniGrav: a drone-deployable miniaturised absolute gravimeter for subsurface mapping
Description: This project will develop a portable prototype that can detect material and structures under the ground. The prototype can be used across a range of fields such as in mining to detect different types of material deposits underground reducing the need for explorative digging as well in defence applications like detection of mines or tunnels. The device is compact enough to be deployed on an unmanned aerial drone or carried by a single soldier.

Title: Blue Ocean LiDAR (laser) for remote ocean temperature mapping
Description: This project aims to commercialise a laser-based method to measure subsurface water temperature and depth that is not currently available commercially. This technology is more efficient than existing approaches (satellite and marine buoys) with broad defence and environmental applications including; detection of underwater objects, increased accuracy in predicting coral bleaching events and refinement to climate modelling.

Title: Revolutionising Radiation Protection: World first multiorgan pharmaceutical radiation protectant for defence capability and civilians
Description: This project aims to commercialise the first drug developed to protect internal organs from radiation sources. If successful the project will have medical and defence applications.

Title: Next-generation stress imaging for rapid structural prototyping, testing and evaluation
Description: This project will enhance the detection of, track, and predict structural fatigue in aircraft. This will enable industry to design more effectively, manufacture, and prototype innovations that result in shorter development cycles and accelerated structural certification for aircraft.

Title: Sovereign Portable Atomic Clock for a Global Positioning System 2.0
Description: This project seeks to reduce the size of atomic clocks in next generation GPS satellites which will result in reduced orbital heights and stronger GPS signals that are more resilient to disruption. These clocks will enhance Australian Defence Capability, allowing Australian defence operations to continue unaffected in GPS-denied or contested international environments.

Title: A novel satellite thermal management system enabling advancement in defence and remote sensing capabilities
Description: This project will apply a new composite 3D printing process to reduce the cost of infrared image acquisition systems in satellites.

Title: Scaling of Advanced Ammunition Manufacturing
University: The University of New South Wales
Description: This project aims to support lower cost mass production of new, high-performance ammunition in different calibres used by the Australian Defence Force (ADF). The project will support sovereign ammunition manufacturing capability, strengthen Australia’s ammunition supply-chain and provide a strategic warfighting and ammunition performance advantage to the ADF.

Title: Pioneering portable labs: user-friendly molecular level COVID test strips
University: The University of New South Wales
Description: This project aims to establish commercial viability of a new type of portable test-strip for COVID-19. These tests will be sensitive enough to replace the current PCR-based COVID-19 testing and will be suitable for use by untrained individuals.

Title: Integrated Rocket Motor Case and Nozzle using Nano- Engineered Phenolic Composite
University: The University of New South Wales
Description: This project aims to develop new carbon composite technology to manufacture integrated single-piece rocket casings, liners, and nozzles. This will reduce the number of rocket failures and support emerging space industries.

Title: Extending radio communications range of Defence platforms through integration of cost-effective functional composite antennas
Description: This project is developing a new antenna prototype that integrates into the wing of an uncrewed plane with improved radio performance that withstands the aerodynamic forces of unmanned flight.

Title: A rapid phase-transition heat absorber by additive manufacturing
Description: This project addresses the growing need in several of Australia’s key industrial sectors to deal with very high heat loads. The project will develop a prototype that controls and absorbs large discharges of thermal energy using 3D-printed components and phase-change materials to rapidly disperse the heat.

Title: Phased Multibeam Antenna Arrays for Autonomous Drones and Surface Vessels
Description: The project will develop a new low-cost, energy efficient antenna technology for autonomous drones and surface vessels as existing solutions are unsuited in power-limited systems (autonomous drones and surface vessels). Additionally, the technology has potential across a range of applications such as enhanced wireless systems for defence, mining automation, intelligent transport, and future communications networks such as 5G and 6G.

Title: Towards passive long-range missile detection based on adaptive multi-spectral mid-wave infrared thermal imaging
Description: This project aims to develop a missile detection system that can be made readily available on a larger array of defence platforms to defend personnel and military assets.

Title: Closed-loop smart cathodic protection technology for infrastructure protection and life extension
Description: The proposed technology will provide protection against corrosion and degradation of critical parts in solar and wind farms.

Title: Methods for the robust employment of metal additive manufacturing in high risk industrial applications
Recipients_Partners: Effusiontech trading as SPEE3D Pty Ltd
Description: The project aims to develop techniques that ensure safe and reliable use of metal additive manufacturing (AM) in high-risk industrial applications by using cold spray and other AM technologies. Currently, the widespread use of AM is hindered due to comprehending quality controls and material properties. Significantly, the project will pioneer the establishment of reliable validation methodologies. The outcomes include the development of new validation techniques, materials and process control methods. The benefits are new possibilities for AM as a viable manufacturing technique without onerous levels of validation and testing thus reducing the effects of supply chain issues in remote areas.

Title: Characterisation of the Aetiology and Prodromal Phase of Parkinson’s Disease in a Novel Murine Model
Description: This project aims to develop a physiologically relevant mouse model of Parkinson’s disease to robustly assess potential efficacy of new treatments for Parkinsons’. Parkinson’s disease is a degenerative brain disorder increasing in prevalence with no cure. Failure to find effective treatments is significantly confounded by a lack of robust preclinical mouse models to efficiently test potential treatments. The outcomes of this project will have a global impact for people living with Parkinson’s disease. The project through the industry partnership will also generate Australian-intellectual property that will be of global interest.

Title: A deep learning method for radiological analysis of spinopelvic mobility
Description: This project aims to using advanced 2D to 3D image reconstruction techniques and artificial intelligence to improve the planning of total hip replacement surgery. The project expects to provide valuable additional information to a surgeon to enhance their surgical decision-making process. This project will enhance the collaboration between 360 MedCare and Flinders University through the application computer vision and deep learning techniques, whilst training the next generation of biomedical engineers. This technology will reduce the risk of dislocation, a major cause of failure of total hip replacements.

Title: Co-design and evaluation of a fully interoperable paediatric burns registry for patients, families and clinicians
Description: This project aims to co-design and implement a paediatric burns registry using automated data capture (ADC) from electronic medical records. It has the potential to improve efficiency and accuracy of data collection for clinical registries, whilst expanding the scope of data collection for national registries to include outpatient data and patient-reported outcome measures. Expected outcomes include a feasible, acceptable and sustainable implementation of a codesigned paediatric burns registry, providing critical insights into paediatric burn care and informing treatment and prevention strategies. The project has the potential to improve paediatric burns outcomes, provide an implementation template of ADC methods for other clinical registries, improve efficiency and effectiveness of observational healthcare research.

Title: Highly sensitive nanosensors for the detection of trace gases in air-based gas mixtures
Description: This project aims to address the agriculture industry's challenge of establishing a non-invasive pregnancy detection system for animals on farms, through the development of advanced gas sensing technologies. The project expects to significantly improve livestock and dairy operator productivity and animal welfare, decrease costs and reduce operator injury. The project will improve gas sensing technology selectivity, fostering a strong research-industry collaboration, and offering the PhD candidate valuable industry insights. This project will revolutionize cattle management across the Meat, Livestock, and Dairy industries, benefiting not only the key industry partner but also various sectors such as food, agriculture, and environmental monitoring.

Title: Decommissioning of mixed-media industrial equipment and opportunities for plastic waste upcycling and recycling in Australia
Description: This project aims to identify and assess pathways for polymer recycling applicable to industrial decommissioned equipment. This project expects to generate a circular materials network within the Australian landscape that links scalable technologies for plastic recycling from university and industry research with the appropriate industrial waste streams and material processing partners. Expected outcomes of this project include a network linking industrial waste to upcycling and recycling partners, which maximises the use of Australia’s most novel and scalable polymer processing technologies. The new recycling network will redirect over 50,000 tonnes of material, destined for landfill, into new products and fuels.

Title: Intelligent Retinal Blood Vessel Analysis on Multiple Imaging Modalities
Description: The project aims to develop advanced artificial intelligence techniques to analyse retinal blood vessels. The project expects to generate new analysis approaches for retinal blood vessels, which are the only visible vessel network in the human body in non-invasive imaging methods. The outcomes of the project will help people understand the relationship between changes in retinal blood vessels and cardiovascular disease. In Australia, 1.2 million people had heart disease and 27% of all deaths are related to diseases of the circulatory system. The project’s outcomes will contribute to cardiovascular disease risk prediction, early detection and disease monitoring.

Title: A Digital Twin Model for Design and Development of Cutting Tools with Macro and Micro Geometries
Description: This project aims to develop a digital twin model of a cutting tool that can incorporate macro and micro geometries. The project expects to develop an accurate and innovative 3D digital model for automated metrology, which is aligned to the core R&D work at Sutton Tools. Expected outcomes include an understanding of the effect of macro and micro tool geometries on cutting tool performance; and development of a digital twin model of a cutting tool that can deliver tool design solutions related to real-world applications. These technologies will benefit rapid development of AI-based approaches for advanced tool design.

Title: Developing a novel cross-protective, inactivated vaccine against non-typeable Haemophilus influenzae
Description: This project aims to develop a new vaccine that will prevent ear infections in children and lung infections in adults. These infections are caused by increasingly common bacteria, Haemophilus influenzae (NTHi). An effective vaccine would reduce the illnesses caused by NTHi, delivering a new Australian product to sell on the global vaccine market. Indigenous communities will also benefit from this vaccine because many children have high rates of middle ear infections caused by NTHi. This project will strengthen collaboration between the University and GPN Vaccines, equipping the PhD candidate with life-long industry-relevant skills and networks, and future career opportunities.

Title: Using machine learning to improve polygenic risk prediction of cancer
Description: This project aims to improve the way that genetic analysis can be used to help predict risk of colorectal cancer. The project will use cutting-edge machine learning techniques to develop new genetic analysis methodologies that are more accurate across a variety of ancestries. The new genetic analysis will be incorporated into Genetic Technologies’ existing colorectal cancer risk prediction test. The new test will better identify people at high risk and enable them to take preventive action or undergo additional screening. This will save lives through early detection of colorectal cancer.

Title: Building Digital Resilience for the climate crisis
Description: The aim of this project is to enable Australian businesses develop innovative digital services that help them adapt to the challenges of climate change and promote environmental sustainability. It is crucial for businesses in Australia to prepare for the impacts of climate change today to achieve net-zero by 2050. The expected outcomes of this project include valuable knowledge, tools, and frameworks that can be used by both technical and non-technical individuals to respond to, and prepare for, climate-related crises. By building digital resilience and helping reduce carbon emissions, this project actively contributes to a more sustainable future for everyone.

Title: Reducing uncertainty and improving the efficiency of driven pile foundation technologies in infrastructure and land development projects
Description: This project aims to investigate how the load capacity of driven pile foundations changes over time. The project expects to generate new approaches to predict this behaviour, as there is no robust methodology that considers the range of influencing variables resulting in inefficiencies and delays when it occurs. Expected outcomes of this project include utilizing the findings in the design of driven foundations, strengthening collaborations and exposing the PhD student to practical foundation engineering. This project will improve efficiency and predictability of driven foundations; benefiting the construction industry and the many public and private projects which rely on piled foundations.

Title: New methods for biomarker discovery from microsampled whole blood of cancer patients
Description: The project aims to develop better ways to diagnose and track the health of cancer patients by using blood samples taken from a fingerpick. The project expects to generate new processes, innovative products and intellectual property for the partners. Expected outcomes of this project include strengthening existing collaborations between university and industry partner and providing the PhD candidate with new scientific research skills. The expected benefits of this project will be to allow consumers to play more active roles in their healthcare by introducing innovative methods for conducting blood tests.

Title: Precision biomanufacturing of postbiotics: the next-generation functional materials for pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, food, and agriculture applications.
Description: Postbiotics are functional molecules produced by probiotics through fermentation and are responsible for the biological effects of probiotics. There is limited knowledge surrounding the physicochemical parameters that affect production of postbiotics. This project will provide fundamental understanding of how the microenvironment of probiotics regulates production and function of postbiotics. The project outcomes will be: (i) commercialisation of Australian-made, sustainably derived functional materials, (ii) highly-skilled workforce and biotechnology experts, and (iii) establishing a resilient academia-industry biomanufacturing ecosystem. Understanding this relationship will enable a paradigm shift from pro- to postbiotics, key to unlocking the full potential of these important functional molecules.

Title: Heritage Equity in Energy Transitions: First Nation cultural heritage protection in extractive mining industries in Australia, Canada and the United States of America
Description: This project will develop new, balanced approaches for the protection of Indigenous cultural heritage, while facilitating the sustainable extraction of Energy Transition Minerals (ETM). Extractive industries represent 10.4% of Australia’s GDP and a staggering 49% of WA’s Gross State Product (2020-1) but operate under deficient frameworks for heritage protection and industry conflict resolution. Expected outcomes include mitigating risks to Indigenous people’s well-being by co-managing impacts to their cultural heritage, reducing risk and industry costs and advancing strategic government priorities. This project will strengthen existing collaborations between industry, Indigenous people, and heritage professionals by providing novel, international best-practice models.

Title: Clinical translation of laser bone sculpting for total knee replacements
Description: The aim of this project is to optimise and verify laser bone shaping parameters, facilitating adoption of this ground-breaking Australian technology into clinical practice. With two million osteoarthritis patients in Australia, the project introduces a novel, patient-centred approach to knee replacements, aimed at improving patient satisfaction and expediting recovery. The project will strengthen academia-industry collaborations, provides a foundation for new partnerships, and develops local expertise for future Australian medical device commercialisation. Laser bone shaping will revolutionize the global practice of orthopaedics, improve patient outcomes, and alleviate strain on public health resources and wait times.

Title: The development of rapid and sensitive methods for the detection of pathogens in water
University: The University of New South Wales
Description: The project aims to develop portable methods to detect pathogenic microorganisms in water samples at the sensitivity level of laboratory gene tests. The new methods will enable onsite and online detection of disease-causing organisms water supplies. The Industry PhD candidate will contribute to the creation of industry-ready portable tests for water safety monitoring. The new designs will be adapted for product development and commercialisation. The outcomes will provide Australia with indigenous capability for portable monitoring of water-borne pathogens and reduce Australia’s reliance on the overseas supply chains for critical biosensing measures.

Title: Development and characterisation of DNA aptamers immobilised on gold electrode surfaces for utility in wearable electrochemical biosensors
University: The University of New South Wales
Description: This project aims to understand how to optimise the function of DNA-based sensing elements when immobilised on electrode surfaces for use with wearable sensors. This is now known to be the crucial step to solving the 50 year old challenge of sensors that can continuously monitor drugs and biomarkers in patients in real time. This will be achieved by using new surface characterisation methods that can show how individual DNA molecules assemble on the electrode and allow the determination how the assembly influences function. This knowledge will accelerate Nutromics’ launch of its wearable biosensor into hospitals and clinics.

Title: TeraStream: Analysing Network Traffic at Terabit Speed using Artificial Intelligence
University: The University of New South Wales
Description: This project aims to provide telecommunications network operators deep visibility into user experience on interactive multimedia applications and cybersecurity threats by utilising novel Programmable Networks and Artificial Intelligence techniques. The project expects to develop innovative network analysis techniques for the partnered Australian enterprise Canopus Networks, addressing Enabling Capabilities priority. Expected outcomes include novel AI systems for user experience and cyber-security, strengthening industrial collaborations, and developing PhD candidate’s skills for translational telecommunications research. This AI-based telecommunications analytics system will provide intellectual property for the Australian industry to maintain its leading position in the telecommunications market globally.

Title: Yeast fermentation and strain optimisation for the Ethtec Cellulosic Ethanol Pilot Plant Project
Description: This project aims to optimise production of bioethanol from agricultural waste, by engineering yeast strains to improve fermentation. The project will generate yeast strains that are efficient in fermenting sugars to products in the shortest time possible, so that the process is economically viable on an industrial scale. Expected outcomes include strengthening the collaboration between the University and Ethanol Technologies, providing excellent training to a PhD student and demonstrating the ability to scale-up fermentations for industrial purposes. This project will produce carbon-neutral bioethanol and green chemicals, offering an alternative to fossil fuels, helping to mitigate climate change impacts.

Title: Durability of concrete/mortar made with recycled Port Augusta fly ash
Description: This project investigates the durability of concrete/mortar made with recycled Port Augusta fly ash, contributing to Hallett Group's Green Cement Transformation Project and advancing sustainable construction practices. The project offers innovative sustainable construction approaches to address a challenge the recycling industry is currently facing, which aligns with industry and government priorities for carbon reduction. The project will provide insights into recycled fly ash concrete/mortar durability and recommendations for its effective use, supporting sustainable construction practices. The practical benefits of the research will include reduction of carbon emissions, deepening industry-academia collaborations, and promoting sustainable practices in the cement and concrete industry.

Title: Performance Evaluation of Eco-friendly Concrete Produced with Granulated lead smelter slag
Description: In partnership with Hallett Group, this project will generate new knowledge about efficient recycling of iron-rich solid waste. This project responds to the global challenge of safe disposal and reuse of lead slag (10–20% of output) due to potential heavy metal leaching and low-use efficiency. The project will develop innovative and cost-effective concrete building materials using lead-zinc slag from Port Pirie smelter to replace cement. Australia, a leading global producer of lead-zinc, will benefit from the availability of more green, economical, and commercially-available methods for producing lead-zinc slag concrete, and new knowledge about efficient recycling and durability performance.

Title: Development of a Chinese herb-drug interaction database: insight into literature, high-throughput screening, mechanism and applications
Description: This project aims to develop an online Evidence-Based Chinese Herb-Drug Database by utilizing laboratory technology and literature reviews. The project expects to generate an advanced digital tool for health care and service in integrative medicine, thereby improving health outcomes and addressing the government’s science and research priorities. Expected outcomes of this project include strengthening existing collaboration between WSU and UnityHealth Pty Ltd. This platform will provide easy access to and reliable information on the integrative use of Chinese herbs, benefiting healthcare professionals, industry, customers, and the public utilising Chinese herbal medicines across Asian Pacific countries.

Title: Understanding animal disease spread by an insect vector in northern Australia
Recipients_Partners: Department of Industry, Tourism and Trade, Northern Territory Government
Description: The project aims to investigate how exotic animal diseases carried by an insect vector could spread in northern Australia. The project expects to develop new approaches to biosecurity surveillance and early detection of exotic animal disease by utilising innovative genomic methods and epidemiological modelling. This project will provide national benefit and support the livestock industry through advancing disease surveillance for animal biosecurity in northern Australia. The expected outcomes of this project include development of skills and capacity in animal biosecurity diagnostics and surveillance and strengthening existing collaborations between the Northern Territory Government and Charles Darwin University.

Title: Prevalence, Prediction and Prevention of spinal pain in rotary wing aircrew
Description: This project aims to reduce the prevalence of spinal injuries in Helicopter aircrew by leveraging past research successes in load monitoring for injury prevention. By reducing spinal injuries, this research will have a direct impact on the Defence Force capabilities by, addressing personnel availability, high training costs, and the negative effects of injuries. The project expects to develop effective strategies for preventing spinal pain, leading to increased personnel availability, reduced training costs, and improved deployable forces. This research will enhance the Defence Force's operational readiness, mitigate financial and personal burdens associated with injuries.

Title: Adaptive Optics Imaging as a Novel Clinical Trial Endpoint for Retinal Gene Therapy
Recipients_Partners: Centre for Eye Research Australia, PYC Therapeutics
Description: This project aims to improve clinical trials for people with inherited retinal diseases by using adaptive optics, a novel imaging technique that monitors disease progression at a cellular level, surpassing previous limitations. Adaptive optics is a new technology that allows accurate evaluation of treatment effectiveness, facilitating faster drug discovery and improved patient care. The project intends to develop new outcome measures to streamline and expedite clinical trials, resulting in better and more cost-effective treatments for patients. Integrating adaptive optics into research advances the understanding of disease progression, leading to targeted therapies and improved clinical care.

Title: Implementation science approaches to promote ocular gene therapy into medical care
Description: This project aims to develop a framework for Australian institutes to deliver ocular gene therapy, encompassing regulatory, organisational, clinician and patient preparedness. This will be achieved by aggregating data, focusing on barriers and enablers to delivering ocular gene therapy. The project will provide an evidence-based model supporting the Australian healthcare system in implementing ocular gene therapy, at the translational interface between research and clinical delivery. Expected outcomes include expanded capacity and capability to deliver ocular gene therapy to patients in Australia. The project will establish a sustainable model for ocular gene therapy, providing sight-saving treatments to Australians at risk of blindness.

Title: Biological predictors of clinical, functional, social and cognitive response to clozapine
Description: This project aims to investigate if brain waves can predict who will respond to clozapine, a treatment for people with schizophrenia. Not everyone with schizophrenia needs clozapine or will get better if they take it. This project is expected to help identify who should be given clozapine and is especially relevant to the industry partner (medical care) who provide care for young people with schizophrenia. Show whether brain waves can predict who will have the best response to clozapine. This project will provide valuable information to improve the lives of young people with schizophrenia.

Title: Artificial intelligence-guided personalized medical and assistive device prescription for improving clinical outcomes and adherence
Description: This project aims to address the issue of generic medical and assistive device prescriptions for patients with diabetic-related foot disease by utilising and advancing artificial intelligence to guide personalised device prescriptions, allowing for individual patient preferences and lifestyles. The project expects to develop an innovative tool for the pedorthic industry, assisting clinicians in prescribing personalised medical devices. Expected outcomes include strengthening existing collaborations with the industry partner and the development of the PhD candidate's skills. This solution will enhance practice for the industry partner, enabling them to better address their patients’ needs and ultimately improve patient adherence and clinical outcomes.

Title: NT rain-fed cotton: predicting yields and saving water
Recipients_Partners: Department of Industry, Tourism and Trade, Northern Territory Government
Description: Australian cotton in the Northern Territory is mainly rain-fed, making it vulnerable to rainfall variations. This project in the Katherine and Douglas-Daly regions uses field data and models to understand water use in rain-fed cotton. Predicting yields under variable rainfall will help strengthen the NT cotton industry and guide water-efficient practices.

Title: Women's engagement and retention in the Northern Territory seafood sector
Recipients_Partners: Fisheries Research and Development Corporation (FRDC), Northern Territory Seafood Council (NTSC), Women in Seafood Australasia (WISA)
Description: This project will investigate ways to enhance the participation and retention of women in the Northern Territory seafood sector, aiming to generate new knowledge and guidance for industry and policy. The research benefits include identification of pathways for an enhanced gender inclusive, robust, and viable sector, with potential national application.

Title: Decision support tool for connecting dSTATCOMs and Battery Energy Storages
Description: This project aims to develop an algorithm to determine the best locations for battery energy storages and other advanced equipment along power lines.  The project aims to ensure that acceptable voltage profiles are maintained when more renewable energy sources are connected to these power lines. Other potential project benefits include improved energy supply to households and industries.

Title: Forensic analysis of home-made explosives for counter-terrorism and forensic intelligence
Description: This project will analyse the chemical composition of homemade explosives with the aim of linking these explosives to their sources. This research will improve the ability of law enforcement officers to conduct counter-terrorism investigations and operations.

Title: Developing blast vibration prediction models using field delay criteria
Description: The project aims to improve mining blast vibration prediction by analysing field cooperate delay with factors like blast design and geology. This research will assist mining companies in predicting and mitigating ground vibrations and safeguarding heritage sites. It will also enhance predictive models, advancing vibration control knowledge.

Title: Health Promotion Housing
Description: This project aims to improve the quality of life of people living in social housing through modular and prefabricated construction, prioritising resident adaptability. Expected outcomes include streamlining construction procedures of social housing and enhancing related programs. The project will be dedicated to developing a health-promoting housing prototype in a rural/regional setting.

Title: Teaching computers to recognise underwater sounds
Description: This research aims to develop efficient, cost-effective methods for a computer to learn and identify maritime objects from acoustic data.  Implementing these methods could automate cost-effective surveillance of Australian shores. The potential benefits of this research include: significantly improving coastal security, monitoring against maritime threats, and aiding maritime exercises.

Title: Physiology-Based Targeted Therapy: Development of the first Pharmacotherapy for Sleep Apnoea
Description: Obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) is a chronic respiratory disorder that affects almost 1 billion people globally. Current device-based treatments are often poorly tolerated or have variable efficiency. This project will use cutting-edge physiology precision medicine approaches to develop the first pharmacotherapy for OSA and identify those most likely to benefit.

Title: Role of evaporative cooling systems in improving indoor air quality
Description: This project will investigate the effect of evaporative cooling systems on indoor microbial air quality. The research aims to determine the potential for evaporative cooling systems to reduce the spread of airborne infectious disease. This information will potentially result in improved indoor air quality and reduce the spread of diseases.

Title: AI-Enhanced Resilient, Efficient, and Cyber-Secure Power Management System
Description: This project will help create a more sustainable and resilient energy landscape. The potential benefits of this research include: contributing to identifying security vulnerabilities in the smart grid; addressing the inefficiency problem for residential power management; improving battery system longevity and performance; and enhancing power consumption prediction.

Title: Queensland grouper: bigger and better through selective breeding
Description: Using advanced genotyping technology, this project will undertake the world’s first selective breeding program of the Queensland Grouper. This research will increase Australian farm productivity and profitability, provide opportunity for new aquaculture entrants, and expand Australia’s competitive reach in international markets.

Title: The ecology and conservation of the threatened Large-eared Pied Bat
Description: This project will combine ecological and genetic approaches to improve understanding of the ecology of one of Australia’s threatened insectivorous bat species, the Large-eared Pied Bat. This project will increase knowledge of the species’ habitat requirements in a changing environment, improving our ability to guide conservation efforts.

Title: Novel cattle feed for reduction of greenhouse gases
Description: This project aims to develop feed additives that can reduce greenhouse gas emissions produced by cattle. If successful, this project will create an anti-methanogenic supplement for use on Australian farms. This could significantly reduce the nation’s greenhouse gas emissions and provide economic benefits to agricultural communities.

Title: Increasing commercialisation success in public research organisations: focusing on healthcare
Recipients_Partners: Hearing Australia through its research division, National Acoustic Laboratories
Description: This project will develop managerial guidelines on how to increase commercialisation success and R&D investment efficiency. This research will help research organisations translate scientific knowledge into new solutions and develop innovation ecosystems.

Title: Converting Food Waste into Compostable Stretch Wrap
Description: This project aims to transform Australian potato waste into compostable stretch wrap using biopolymers generated by waste-consuming bacteria. Success in this project offers a sustainable solution for the next generation of compostable pallet films, promoting a circular economy, reducing petroleum-based plastics reliance and curbing plastic waste in landfills and oceans.

Title: Green future quest: teamwork for a cleaner world
Description: This project is dedicated to finding the most efficient clean energy and anti-pollution technologies. The goal is to assist businesses and governments to make eco-friendly and cost-effective technology choices, thus reducing pollution and saving money.

Title: Electric Vehicle Tariff and Feed-in-tariff Design for Smart Charger Implementation
University: The Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology (RMIT)
Description: This project will develop methodologies to calculate appropriate payment rates for electric vehicle charging in public charging stations. The expected outcome of the project is a set of market-based rules to determine the variable electric vehicle charging rates. This project will benefit both electric vehicle and charging station owners.

Title: Helping cultural institutions create digital environments reflective of audience neurodiversity
University: The Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology (RMIT)
Description: This project will develop ways for galleries, libraries, archives and museums to make digital content more accessible for people identifying as neurodivergent by developing new guidelines, content environments and a design methods toolkit. Potential benefits include fuller access and greater participation in cultural heritage for people identifying as neurodiverse.

Title: Tailored support for Aboriginal children in out-of-home care
Recipients_Partners: Abcare (Coffs Harbour Aboriginal Family Community Care Centre Aboriginal Corporation)
Description: This project will create a psycho-education and support program for Aboriginal children in out-of-home care. It has the potential to increase engagement with support services, contributing to evidence-based policies and practices in child welfare.

Title: Low-cost lenses for thermal imaging
Description: The project aims to make new, lower-cost lenses for use in thermal imaging cameras, security systems, smart phones, and home appliances.

Title: Advanced Silicon Carbide Transistor Prototype for Highly Efficient and Reduced Cost Power Conversion Systems
Description: This project aims to develop an advanced Silicon Carbide (SiC) semiconductor switch for use in smaller, lighter, cost-effective and highly efficient renewable energy generation systems such as those used in electric vehicles.

Title: Pitting AI Against Phone Scams – A Proactive Defence
Description: This project aims to undermine scam callers by developing a technology that will redirect scam calls to conversational AI bots optimised to present as convincing scam victims.

Title: All-electronic sensing platform for real-time stand-off detection of toxic gases
Description: The project will develop prototypes for portable, lightweight, low-cost sensors for real-time detection of toxic gases in hard to reach places. This sensor technology will ensure the safety and efficacy of environmental monitoring undertaken by workers across a range of industries from mining, chemical processing to food safety.

Title: Personalised aerosol therapy: enabling inhaled administration of next generation therapeutics
Description: This project will develop a personalised aerosol drug therapy system to enable inhalation of a broader range of biological therapeutics.

Title: Towards Sustainable Agriculture: Development of a Robotic Harvesting System
Description: This project will develop a robotic arm for an apple-harvesting robot that will improve harvest yield and promote Australia's technological competence in the emerging agricultural harvesting robot market.

Title: Development of recombinant plasminogen fusion proteins for wound healing and diseases associated with fibrin accumulation
Description: The project aims to develop a blood-clot dissolving protein for chronic conditions that promotes wound healing and limits scarring of tissue. The project aims to apply the protein to assist in cases of stroke, chronic inflammation and fibrosis.

Title: FeBI – Advancing quantum technology to transform the diagnosis and management of iron disorders
Description: This project will develop a new blood test based on quantum sensing that improves diagnostic sensitivity and management of iron related disorders.

Title: Converged architecture of millimetre-wave wireless communications and edge computing for transformation of advanced manufacturing environments
Description: The project aims to uplift Australian manufacturing through digital transformation of plants and factories. The project will improve wireless network connectivity in advanced manufacturing settings improving productivity, cutting waste, and making manufacturing processes more competitive.

Title: Dynamic interface printing as a novel biofabrication technology
Description: This project aims to develop a new biological 3D printing prototype as a potential alternative to the use of animal tissue in patients. The technology would allow medical practitioners to fabricate artificial organ and tissue models using human cells. This project aims to rapidly print tissues within seconds, to develop accurate, cost-effective, and clinically viable treatments.

Title: Commercialising a Wideband Quantum Microwave Amplifier
University: The University of New South Wales
Description: This project seeks to commercialise a quantum-enabled device that boosts the strength of weak communication signals. The ‘quantum amplifier’ can be used in applications where the detection of very weak microwaves is critical, such as in quantum computing, satellite communication, defence and fundamental scientific research.

Title: Miniaturising and up-scaling of robotic tactile sensors with CMOS photonic pixel arrays
University: The University of New South Wales
Description: This project will aim to improve the usability and capability of agricultural robots that deliver higher yields and less damage to products.

Title: Pilot-scale manufacture of microfluidic bioreactors for the biotech industry
University: The University of New South Wales
Description: The biotech industry relies on large-scale fermentation methods to scale-up biopharmaceutical products. However, products that modify patients’ own cells to treat disease are too expensive to manufacture at scale using this method. This project will develop a process, using additive manufacturing techniques, to automate complex cell manufacturing processes at a reduced cost to test and evaluate the feasibility of automation at larger volumes.

Title: Development of a commercial version of a software model checker
University: The University of New South Wales
Description: The project will develop a new software verification system that identifies and mitigates errors and security concerns in new software. The software has broad applicability across several sectors including defence, computer hardware, avionics, automotive, robotics, autonomous systems and blockchain to provide assurance of digital systems.

Title: Commercialisation of an anticorrosion coating technology for underground mine applications
University: The University of New South Wales
Description: This project aims to develop a new anti-corrosion coating technology for bolts used in mining operations that will improve worker safety and reduce the cost of maintenance and repair.

Title: Automated Robotic System for Seamless Manufacturing of Polymeric Heart Valve Replacements with Enhanced Longevity and Possibility for Personalisation
Description: This project aims to advance the development of next generation heart valve replacements with a fully automated robotic manufacturing system. The system will efficiently produce customised valves for each patient and have an extended lifespan of over 25 years.

Title: A sovereign Autonomous Underwater Vehicle capability
Description: The project will test an Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (AUV) that can hover above the seafloor to collect better data in difficult conditions. This technology could be used for environmental surveys of offshore infrastructure assessments (such as windfarms), scientific data collection and various defence applications.

Title: Bulk, through-put enantiomer separation using helical electromagnetic devices for pharmaceutical manufacturing
Description: This project will develop a new device to improve the process of separating molecules which is a costly and time-consuming process for pharmaceutical development. Success of this project will reduce drug manufacturing costs.

Title: Rotation Testing Low-cost Gyroscopes for Autonomous Land Navigation
Description: This project will test a new type of laser-based sensor for use in land navigation technology used in self-driving cars. The project aims to meet the strict safety standards for the automotive industry at a lower price point for consumers.

Title: A new method for commercial ship route optimisation using real-time ocean intelligence
University: The University of New South Wales
Description: This project aims to commercialise a new digital technology that optimises cargo vessels’ transit time to minimise fuel consumption. The technology will utilise state-of-the-art ocean forecast models, machine learning, and mathematical techniques to compare hundreds of thousands of possible routes in minutes to inform each vessel of a fuel-efficient navigation option.

Title: New Hydrogen Fuel Cell for Aviation Transportation
University: The University of New South Wales
Description: This project aims to develop a new fuel cell to power small drones and assist the aviation transport sector in developing clean aircraft that are low-cost, low-weight and high-range.

Title: Developing a Novel High- Efficiency Micro-Electric Vehicle Motor
University: The University of New South Wales
Description: The project will develop and validate a prototype Australian e-bike motor that will use 40% less rare-earth material. This project aims to reduce production cost, power consumption, lower audible noise and make e-Bikes lighter and therefore more efficient.

Title: Music Attuned Technology Care via eHealth (MATCH) A music adaptive technology and training program to manage dementia symptoms
Description: Currently more than 55 million people have dementia worldwide, over 60% of whom live in low-and middle-income countries. Every year, there are nearly 10 million new cases. This project aims to create a music system that specifically targets dementia and enhances the overall quality of life for individuals affected by this condition. Additionally, this project recognises the importance of providing training for caregivers, enabling them to effectively utilise the technology and support individuals with dementia, improving the well-being of individuals and their caregivers.

Title: A novel framework for automated design of personalised implants
Description: Fracture plates for internal fixation of fractures have been used for more than a hundred years.  However, while these plates improve patient outcomes, they are still considered blunt in their application. This project aims to progress novel software called ‘AutoPlate3D’ capable of automating the design and production of personalised fracture plates to better match patients’ specific needs. This software will enhance the efficiency, accuracy and customisation of fracture plate production, allowing for industrial manufacturing in Australia and ultimately improving patient care in the treatment of fractures.

Title: A novel microfluidic device for ocular tear fluid collection
Description: Dry eye disease affects around 20% of adult Australians and costs the economy close to $1.2 billion a year in care and treatment. This project aims to develop a tear collector device that is crucial for the functioning of a tear diagnostic platform known as ADMiER, capable of effectively and efficiently diagnosing dry eye disease. Unlike current methods, this device has the potential to transform the field of ophthalmology through non-invasive diagnosis. The device will also provide clinicians with valuable insights into the underlying causes and appropriate treatment strategies, leading to rapid and precise care for patients.

Title: Enhancing biopharmaceuticals: a disruptive bioseparation resin technology
Description: This project's goal is to progress groundbreaking resin technology for the large-scale production of complex medicines made from living cells or organisms, known as biopharmaceuticals. This technology will address bioseparation limitations experienced by the biopharmaceutical manufacturing industry. Bioseparation refers to the process of separating and purifying biological molecules, such as proteins, from a complex mixture to produce a high-quality product for therapeutic use. The project involves developing bacterial cell factories that can produce a high-quality resin efficiently and affordably, which will transform the production of blood plasma-medicines.

Title: Highly efficient and simplified hydrogen compression with metal hydrides
Description: Hydrogen is a clean fuel of high energy density, however as it is a gas it has a low volumetric density. This project aims to advance the integration of advanced materials, specifically hydrides, into hydrogen compressors to achieve the efficient and maintenance-free storage of hydrogen. This initiative is significant as it addresses the need for more efficient storage solutions, which is a critical component in the broader adoption of the clean energy source. Such novel metal hydride-based compressors will enable a greater deployment of hydrogen to directly refill fuel cell vehicles and on industrial sites to decarbonise the hard to abate sectors including the steel, cement and chemical industry. The successful integration of advanced materials into hydrogen compressors could lead to more cost effective and space efficient storage methods, supporting the transition to net zero.

Title: Development of an intraoral robotic device for enhancing tooth restoration
Description: While automation and robotic assistance are widely adopted in other medical fields, their application in dentistry remains limited. Dentists rely heavily on their eyesight and dexterity to perform complex restorative and aesthetic procedures. This project aims to create small robotic devices for the dental industry, capable of effectively and painlessly removing diseased teeth. The miniature robotic device has the potential to revolutionise the dental industry by offering efficient treatment options and patient comfort.

Title: The Rectangular Block Dental Implant. Prototype to the Clinic
Description: Affordable and effective dental surgery can have long lasting impacts on a range of patient health outcomes. Where preventative measures are not enough, restorative dentistry is necessary to assist patients. This project aims to tackle the challenges associated with placing dental implants (replacements for missing teeth) in patients who are not suitable candidates for conventional implant procedures. By addressing challenges like low bone volume in older patients, the project aims to expand the accessibility and effectiveness of dental implant treatments, particularly for individuals who may have been previously precluded from receiving such implants.

Title: A safe, affordable, and durable battery technology for fully decarbonized electric grid
University: The University of New South Wales
Description: Aqueous zinc batteries, with their safety, sustainability and cost-effective production, are ideal for large-scale renewable every storage. The aim of this project is to enhance the durability and energy density of aqueous zinc batteries, with the focus on improving the overall performance and stability at harsh temperature conditions. The project benefits, including advanced battery technology development and manufacturing, will foster job creation, skills development, and value add to materials resources, leading to long-term economic growth and prosperity. An affordable, safe and recyclable battery technology for residential, commercial and grid-scale storage could accelerate widespread renewable implementation, supporting Australia's transition to net zero.

Title: An Internet of Things platform for smart farming through new truly simple and affordable soil moisture sensors: A shallow install for deep root crops
Description: This project aims to develop a simple and smart soil monitoring system to support data-driven decision making in agriculture. This monitoring system will de-risk farm operations and encourage more sustainable practices that reduce irrigation and fertiliser use, helping to optimise sowing practices and limit crop losses. This system is designed to be affordable and accurate, capable of measuring soil moisture and temperature to depths of up to 2 meters from 15 centimetres depth installation. These outcomes will support growth in Australia’s agricultural sector with projections indicating $514 million annual savings if the system was adopted by Australia’s 11,000 wheat and barley farms alone.
